summary.headline: EMS Ltd Q1 FY27 standalone operating income rose about 50% QoQ to Rs 125.72 crore, with PAT of Rs 15.03 crore and Rs 317 crore of new work orders.
summary.overview: Management reported standalone operating income of Rs 125.72 crore, up about 50% QoQ, with EBITDA margin of 25.53% and PAT of Rs 15.03 crore. Consolidated operating income was Rs 157.24 crore, up about 30%, with consolidated PAT of Rs 15.49 crore. Management attributed the weak prior quarters to monsoon disruption in Uttarakhand and election-related restrictions in West Bengal (Kolkata), which left fixed establishment costs uncovered. Management guided FY27 revenue back to roughly Rs 900-950 crore, with Q2 about 30-35% above Q1 and Q4 the strongest quarter.

financial_highlights.metric: PAT margin (Q1 FY27, as stated by H.K. Kansal)

segments.name: Kolkata / West Bengal sewerage project
segments.commentary: Execution was hit by election-related restrictions. Management said the Rs 70-80 crore run rate is not expected before Q3, as sewer line revenue cannot be booked quickly; Q3 and Q4 are expected to be stronger.

segments.name: Uttarakhand
segments.commentary: Heavy monsoon rains and a state directive halting sewerage work delayed execution in prior quarters; ramp-up started in Q3/Q4 FY26. Management stated about 61% of revenue came from Uttarakhand in the current period (as stated on the call).

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: Management stated about 42% of revenue came from Uttar Pradesh in the current period (as stated on the call).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue targeted at roughly Rs 900-950 crore, similar to FY25 levels; management said this is 'at par' with FY25 by year-end.
Q2 FY27 revenue expected about 30-35% above Q1; Q3 and Q4 expected to grow more than 50% QoQ, with Q4 the strongest and Q2 the weakest of the remaining three quarters.
Management said margins should return to around 25% EBITDA and 15% PAT, citing margin-accretive order book; it noted margins may settle slightly below FY24 levels due to rising competition.
Management said FY27 would grow at least 50% over FY26 (about Rs 125 crore already achieved in Q1, per Ashish Tomar).
No capex plan as of now, per management.
capex_capacity: No capex or investment plan for FY27 as of now, per Ashish Tomar.
Fixed costs (establishment, labour, machinery rent) mean margins compress when revenue dips, per H.K. Kansal.
demand_pricing: Work orders of about Rs 317 crore converted in Q1 FY27 from the Delhi and Maharashtra bidding pipeline (cited as Rs 2,500-3,000 crore).
About Rs 158 crore of additional work orders received in Q2 to date; L1 position on a Banaras project above Rs 100 crore.
Bidding in Bihar and Madhya Pradesh; exploring Maharashtra and Karnataka.
Management said competition is increasing, so margins may not return fully to FY24 levels.
Management said current order book was bid at margins similar to target levels.

qa_highlights.question: Has West Bengal execution reached the Rs 70-80 crore run rate after election restrictions were lifted?
qa_highlights.answer: Restrictions are lifted, but the run rate will only be achieved from Q3 because sewer line revenue cannot be booked quickly; Q3 and Q4 Kolkata numbers expected to be much better.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 2,500-3,000 crore pipeline has reached award?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 317 crore converted to work orders in Q1, Rs 158 crore more received in Q2 to date, and L1 on a Banaras project above Rs 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of margin compression and how will it be reversed?
qa_highlights.answer: Monsoon disruptions and government restrictions reduced revenue while fixed establishment, labour and machinery costs stayed; margins rise with revenue. Management said PAT margin went from 6.3% in Q4 FY26 to 11.95% in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital stretched and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Government payment delays slow work, which delays billing; management said working capital needs are about 120 days of turnover (about Rs 300-350 crore on Rs 1,000 crore turnover).

qa_highlights.question: How long does conversion from order to revenue take?
qa_highlights.answer: Engineering and approvals take about six months after work order; site revenue starts around 8-9 months after award, with total timelines of 18-24 months of revenue conversion on two-to-three-year projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue split and how much will the Rs 2,329 crore order book execute this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 50% growth over FY26 and said Rs 125 crore is already achieved in Q1, with the balance in the remaining quarters; it stated Rs 300 crore of revenue in Q3-Q4 is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue concentration by state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 42% of revenue from Uttar Pradesh and about 61% from Uttarakhand for the current period, which together exceed 100%, so the basis needs clarification.

risks_watch: Monsoon and government restrictions (Uttarakhand, West Bengal) have repeatedly stalled execution; Q2 is the rainy season and management expects only 30-35% QoQ growth.
Working capital cycle around 120 days; delayed government payments are slowing work and billing.
Revenue target of Rs 900-950 crore needs roughly Rs 250-300 crore in each of the remaining quarters, with about Rs 300 crore in Q3-Q4 combined per the analyst's math, which management confirmed.
Margin recovery to 25% EBITDA and 15% PAT is management's target, not yet demonstrated; rising competition may cap margins below FY24 levels.
High state concentration (Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand); the disclosed percentages need confirmation.
Management said Q1 numbers were partly seasonal; the analyst pushed for YoY comparisons rather than QoQ.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the recovery and the FY27 revenue target, but defensive on margin compression and execution delays, which management attributed to weather, government restrictions and fixed costs. Answers on working capital and state-wise revenue were loose and some figures were restated during the call.
